content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I am trying to run an online test on a [product_name] 24V module using [product_name] V7, but I keep encountering a 'Transmission failed' error. My PC doesn't have a built-in COM port, so I'm using a USB-RS232 adapter. Should I adjust the Baud rate settings? Also, how can I manually set values?

Hi, Based on my experience, even when you use a USB-RS232 adapter, Windows still assigns a COM port. Here's what to do: 1. Disconnect your USB adapter from the computer. 2. Open the Control Panel, go to Device Manager, and check the Ports (COM & LPT) section. 3. Reconnect the USB adapter; you should see a new COM port appear. This is the virtual COM port for your adapter. Select this COM port number in [product_name] (via Tools > Options > Interface). You can try 'Automatic Detection,' but finding the right virtual COM port can sometimes take a while. After configuring this, you should be able to start the online test in [product_name]. This method works well on my PC. I've attached some images that show the process in detail. Hope it helps.
Just to clarify: I read that with a program in LAD format, online simulation is not possible, but with FBD format, online testing works. Is this accurate?
Hello, According to the official documentation, the circuit program being tested can be in either FBD or LAD format, but it must be transferred to the [product_name] device. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced issues with online testing using [product_name] V7, mainly due to communication errors involving a USB-RS232 adapter and uncertainty regarding simulation mode compatibility (LAD vs FBD). Clarification from documentation confirmed that both circuit formats are supported for testing once transferred to the device.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable device communication for online testing, accurate guidance on simulation format compatibility, and easy setup when using newer computer hardware interfaces.
